en: The lawyer takes something else from the case. The contract is not a pathological exception but the legal form in which the structure puts itself in writing, and the denial of value it contains does not decide whether the loss is legally relevant, because it tries to collapse by definition what in practice functions as accumulated immaterial assets. The problem translates into the factual vulnerability of Article 4, item I, of the CDC<1><2>1</2></1>, which justifies heightened duties of transparency, loyalty and information.

<1><2>3</2><3>How the platform extracts value</3><4>Platform consumption tends to be organized around a business model that extracts value from control of access, from manufactured scarcity and from the consumer's own presence, and this model explains supplier conduct that reading a clause in isolation cannot reach. Read with Varoufakis, Dowbor and Marx, the model gives the jurist conditions of attribution, and not a condemnation of the market.</4></1>

In ecosystems in which enjoyment is prepared by cycles of anticipation, advertising and the offer cannot be treated as an external, ornamental or legally neutral layer. In many of these objects, the offer is not limited to the final purchase statement and is built progressively through an economy of signs that precedes enjoyment and conditions how the consumer interprets what is acquired. Teasers, which are short pieces of advance communication, storefronts, previews, countdowns, suggestions of rarity, insinuated equivalences and promises of prestige, belonging or performance make up the program of the offer insofar as they take part in forming legitimate expectation. The basic rule is in Article 30 of the CDC<1><2>4</2></1>, under which all sufficiently precise information or advertising binds the supplier and becomes part of the contract. This holds with special force when the utility is mediated by interface, visual presentation and promises of progression, and the offer does not disappear after adhesion. Rizzatto Nunes recognizes that the offer can arise from the mere presentation of the product in the storefront, which supports reading the digital storefront as a binding offer.

The objectives in Article 3, items I and III, of the Constitution<1><2>5</2></1>, of building a free, just and solidary society and of reducing inequalities, rule out any constitutional neutrality in favor of private arrangements that deepen structural dependencies under the pretext of efficiency or innovation, and Bruno Miragem adds that consumer protection shapes the legitimate functioning of economic activity without depending on the supplier's tolerance. Property too is subject to its social function, under Article 5, item XXIII, of the Constitution<3><4>6</4></3>, and José Afonso da Silva shows that the social function bears on the very content of the right, its recognition and its guarantee, so that the social function is an internal element of legitimacy and not a peripheral correction. Fábio Konder Comparato shows that this containment is not an isolated innovation of recent constitutionalism, because the development of economic, social and cultural rights led to the recognition that private parties too have the duty to respect human rights. Governed enjoyment thus activates functional limits on private positions founded on exclusivity and technical control.

The dynamic distribution provided for in Article 373, paragraph 1, of the CPC<1><2>22</2></1> depends on a reasoned decision. Redistribution does not eliminate the need for plausibility, for a coherent chain of argument and for delimiting the disputed object. What it eliminates is the fiction of symmetry.
